units.title: Class II, III, IV and V Antiarrhythmic Map
units.sec: Class II, III, IV and V Antiarrhythmic Map · p74
units.guide: Part 2 re-lists the non-class-I antiarrhythmics. Class II contains β blockers; class III contains K+ blockers including bretylium, dofetilide, ibutilide, vernakalant, amiodarone and sotalol; class IV contains diltiazem/verapamil; and class V contains adenosine, MgSO4, atropine and digoxin. This opening map anchors the later details on AV nodal block, K+ blockade and miscellaneous drugs.

units.title: Class II β Blockers and Class IV Calcium Channel Blockers
units.sec: Class II β Blockers and Class IV Calcium Channel Blockers · p74
units.guide: Class II and class IV drugs both cause relative AV nodal block when used individually. β blockers are used for SVT/PSVT, idiopathic VT with reduced heart rate, ventricular premature beats and catecholamine-induced arrhythmias from pheochromocytoma or halothane. Diltiazem/verapamil are used for SVT/PSVT, but class II and IV must never be combined because total conduction block can result.

units.title: Class III K+ Channel Blockers and Amiodarone Spectrum
units.sec: Class III K+ Channel Blockers and Amiodarone Spectrum · p74
units.guide: Class III drugs delay ventricular repolarization, producing QT prolongation and torsades risk. Ibutilide has the maximum torsades risk, whereas amiodarone has minimum torsades risk because it blocks K+, Na+, β and Ca2+ channels. Amiodarone is the broadest and longest-acting antiarrhythmic; ibutilide is the shortest-acting K+ blocker used IV for acute fibrillation/flutter attacks.

units.title: Amiodarone Adverse Effects and Dronedarone
units.sec: Amiodarone Adverse Effects and Dronedarone · p75
units.guide: Amiodarone toxicity is dominated by iodine-related lung, liver, skin, thyroid and ocular problems. Pulmonary fibrosis needs baseline X-ray/PFT and is contraindicated in ILD; corneal deposits are whorl-like, usually asymptomatic and reversible; skin effects include ceruloderma and brown photosensitive pigmentation; and thyroid disease is more often hypothyroid in plain dwellers than hyperthyroid in hilly areas. Dronedarone lacks iodine, so it is less toxic but also less efficacious.

units.title: Adenosine: MOA, Route, Dosing and Uses
units.sec: Adenosine: MOA, Route, Dosing and Uses · p76
units.guide: Adenosine acts on adenosine receptors to block the AV node through Gi, cause bronchoconstriction through Gq and vasodilate through Gs. Because it is rapidly taken up into cells and degraded orally by gastric acid, it must be given as an IV rapid push—6 mg, then 12 mg if there is no response. It is DOC for acute SVT/PSVT after vagal/carotid massage and can maintain controlled hypotension during surgery.

units.title: Adenosine Adverse Effects, Digoxin and Magnesium Sulfate
units.sec: Adenosine Adverse Effects, Digoxin and Magnesium Sulfate · p76
units.guide: Adenosine commonly causes transient apnea and flushing; it may trigger atrial fibrillation by K+ channel opening and is contraindicated in asthma/COPD, atrial fibrillation and transplanted hearts because of denervation hypersensitivity. Digoxin blocks the AV node and is used as a chronic CHF inotrope plus SVT/PSVT drug. MgSO4 blocks Ca2+ channels to shorten QT and is DOC for acute torsades; congenital long QT is managed with β blockers and pacing, while acquired drug-induced long QT requires avoiding drugs.
